cfb.award_narrative.label: Award candidates (Heisman) production and narrative
cfb.award_narrative.measurement: Candidate stats and team rank, historical winners model, odds path, ballot timeline; update weekly.
cfb.award_narrative.mechanism: Awards like the Heisman follow production, team success, QB/position bias and narrative in an electorate that is known and timed.
cfb.award_narrative.rationale: Winners are mostly QBs on top-ranked teams; narrative changes weekly; ballots close before certain late games.

cfb.award_vote_feature_model.label: Award-specific vote-share model features
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.measurement: For each award and year since 2010 fit a multinomial logit of vote share on: rank of the candidate's primary counting stat among the position pool (percentile), team win percentage and AP rank at ballot time, games played fraction, prior-year honours, and a position-group indicator; regularise with ridge (lambda chosen by leave-year-out); produce candidate probabilities with ties handled by 1/N rule where voters can share an award. Ballot date as-of cut.
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.mechanism: Candidate-level features that predict vote share for each award: counting stats, team record, ranking, position bias and highlight games.
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.rationale: Different awards have different electorates and different positional constraints: the Biletnikoff goes to a receiver, AP defensive player awards to defenders, and voters see box-score numbers and team results rather than efficiency grades; a position-agnostic Heisman narrative variable misses all of this.

cfb.ballot_points_gap.label: Ballot points and first-place vote state
cfb.ballot_points_gap.measurement: From each weekly AP release record points and first-place votes for ranks 1 to 5; compute share = points_i / (62 x 25 +... ) using ballot count n of that week; gap = (points_1 - points_2) / total points possible; successor probability = softmax over ranks 2-5 with temperature fitted on historical handovers (n about 50 events). As-of the latest published poll.
cfb.ballot_points_gap.mechanism: Points and first-place votes of the top teams as published, giving the margin by which the leader leads the next team.
cfb.ballot_points_gap.rationale: If the number-one team loses, the successor is the team with the next-most points unless voters coalesce around a winner; a large first-place vote share for the number two team means a quick handover, and a small gap leads to a split and possibly a different team ascending, which controls the count of distinct number-one teams.
raw_data: weekly AP points and first-place votes

cfb.bowl_selection_state.label: Bowl eligibility, slot balance and conference tie-in selection model
cfb.bowl_selection_state.measurement: Per simulation of the season (the cfb.rating_posterior_draws and remaining-game win probabilities), compute each team regular-season wins, flag eligibility at >=6 wins (and, for 5-7 teams, an APR-ranked fallback list), count eligible teams per conference, allocate teams to bowl slots by the season tie-in table (conference, pick order, bowl slot count 2026 list from the rules text) with a selection score of wins, rank and historical draw (seed to be fitted on bowl selections 2014-2025), and remove the CFP field first. Output P(selected) per team and per-conference shortage probability of eligible teams below slots. Re-run weekly; the bowl list is the one in the contract text.
cfb.bowl_selection_state.mechanism: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME settles on being selected (not playing) for a certified Division I bowl or the CFP: the chain is 6-win eligibility, the count of eligible teams against bowl slots, conference tie-in order, bowl committee choices and top teams taken by the CFP.
cfb.bowl_selection_state.rationale: Selection is not a function of wins alone: when eligible teams (6 or more wins) exceed slots, the weakest eligible teams miss out; when slots exceed eligible teams, 5-7 teams are taken (typically ranked by APR, a rule that changes by season); a conference with more eligible teams than tie-ins sends the surplus to open slots with bowls choosing by expected draw and travel, so a 6-6 mid-major is a bubble case while a 7-5 power team is safe.
raw_data: bowl tie-in table by conference and year

cfb.bubble_proximity_state.label: Top-25 bubble proximity (others receiving votes and ranks 20-30)
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.measurement: At each release collect points for ranks 15-25 and the unranked others receiving votes list (typically 10-20 teams with points); for each team compute z = (team points - points at rank 25) / SD of week-to-week points change (fitted); P(ranked next week) = Phi(z + expected effect of the coming game from the transition model). For CFP exact-rank: density of resume-metric gaps around ranks 22-28. As-of latest release.
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.mechanism: Points of unranked teams receiving votes and the gap among teams ranked 20 to 30, for entry and exact-rank markets near the cut line.
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.rationale: Contracts such as top 25 in AP Week 5 or exactly #25 in the CFP rankings sit on the boundary where many teams have similar resumes and tiny vote differences decide placement; probabilities depend on the density of teams around the cut line rather than on the strength of the team in question alone.
raw_data: weekly AP points for ranks 1-25 and others

cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.measurement: Fit an ordered-response or rank regression for each committee release 2014 to latest: rank ~ ESPN Strength of Record or equivalent resume metric (computed from own ratings if unavailable), number of wins over top-25 and top-50 opponents, losses (count and margin), head-to-head, conference-champion flag, previous week rank (inertia coefficient), and week index; evaluate by rank error and by the probability of making the field. cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.mechanism: Predicted committee rank from record, strength of record, quality wins and losses, conference champion status and previous ranking.
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.rationale: Playoff berth, seed and top-N ranking contracts are decided by a committee, not by the ratings: the committee emphasises wins over ranked teams and conference championships, penalises losses depending on opponent and timing, and moves slowly week to week. A rating-only model misses the selection layer.

cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.label: CFP committee ranking features and protocol
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.measurement: Fit a rank model on the 2014 to latest committee releases: rank_t ~ rank_(t-1), ESPN SOR or own resume metric, number of wins over top-25 and top-50 teams, losses (count, margin, quality), conference champion flag (post-title game), head-to-head vs adjacent teams, injury flag for starting quarterback; output the rank distribution at the release date (Nov 24). cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.label: Buyout exposure and contract state
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.measurement: For each head coach: buyout amount B(t) as a function of date from contract terms (stepdowns on dates such as Jan 1 or Jun 30), mitigated by offset clauses; ratio = B(t) / (annual athletic revenue + booster fund proxy); record the ratio at the as-of date and at the window end. Missing contracts imputed with the 3-year median for the conference tier.
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.mechanism: Remaining contractually-secured pay and buyout owed by the school, expressed relative to athletic department finances, as a function of date.
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.rationale: The firing decision is partly financial: a school owing 30 to 80 million dollars is far less likely to fire before a contractual step-down; buyouts often fall after December 31 or at the start of a contract year, so timing within the window matters.

cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.label: Head-coach exit hazard features
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.measurement: Cox proportional hazard by week with features: wins minus preseason expected wins from non-market ratings (to date), consecutive losses, losses to rivals, remaining contractually-secured buyout in dollars relative to athletic department revenue, tenure and age (retirement), athletic director tenure (first-year AD indicator), outside-job interest flag; fit on FBS head-coach changes 2005-2025 (about 15-25 per year); output cumulative probability for each specific window end (Dec 1, Feb 1) given as-of date. Competing risks: fit cause-specific hazards for (a) fired, (b) resigns or retires (age, health, announced future departure counts under COACHLEAVE/COACHOUT), (c) leaves for another program or the NFL (poached; outside-job interest flag, assistant-coach and peer-vacancy market) while an interim appointment is non-qualifying for NEXTCOACH. Prior-only fallback: until the covariate model validates on held-out years (it cannot be validated with 15-25 changes a year and a dozen features), the default forecast is the calendar-window base rate from cfb.offfield_base_rate adjusted only by wins minus expectation; covariates enter only if they improve out-of-sample log loss.
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.mechanism: Covariates of the weekly probability that a head coach is fired, resigns or announces departure: record versus expectation, contract and buyout, losing streaks, rivalry results, age and administration stability.
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.rationale: Both COACHLEAVE and COACHOUT resolve on leaving or announcing departure within a window, and the hazard is concentrated at the end of the regular season and after bowls; the cost of firing (buyout) restrains exits, while a deep disappointment relative to expectation, athletic director turnover or an attractive outside job raises them.

cfb.coach_overperformance_index.label: Coach overperformance index
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.measurement: Expected wins from non-market preseason rating and schedule (Poisson-binomial of game win probabilities) minus actual wins to date plus projected remaining wins; add change in AP rank from preseason to ballot date and a conference-title indicator; fit historical Coach of the Year winners 2005-2025 with a logit on the index, final record, final ranking, and first-year/turnaround flags. As-of ballot date.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.mechanism: Wins above preseason expectation and rank change for a head coach's team, from non-market preseason ratings.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.rationale: Coach of the Year voting rewards teams that exceed expectations, not simply the best team; a coach who takes a team expected to win 5 to 11 wins is favoured over one at the top of the polls, but ranking and conference title also matter.

cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.label: Conference schedule grid and correlated win-count simulation inputs
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.measurement: For each conference, take the 2026 schedule as of the as-of date: for every game g compute P(home win) from a non-market rating difference (cfb.sp_plus or own rating) plus venue term, with each team rating drawn once per simulation from N(rating, cfb.rating_posterior_sd^2) and a conference-level shift drawn from N(0, tau_c^2) with tau_c estimated from the historical dispersion of cross-conference results (start tau_c=1.5 points, to be fitted). Simulate 20,000 seasons, count teams with >=10 regular-season wins (FCS opponents count as wins) and read P(count>=K). Re-run weekly using results to date as fixed; report the simulated count variance against the independent-Poisson-binomial variance as a diagnostic.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.mechanism: For the count-of-teams-with-10+-wins contracts: the conference game grid (who plays whom, home/away, byes) plus non-conference opponents define each team win probability vector, and shared rating uncertainty plus intra-conference head-to-head games make team outcomes dependent.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.rationale: The count is not a Poisson-binomial of independent teams: every intra-conference game gives one team a win and another a loss, so wins are negatively dependent within the conference, while a shared conference-strength error (cross-conference calibration) makes them positively dependent. The two forces change the variance of the count and therefore the tail rung (5+ Big 12, 7+ Big Ten, 8+ SEC). Regular season only, so championship games and bowls are excluded from the count.
raw_data: conference schedule grid by season (team, opponent, site, week)

cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.label: Conference membership, schedule format and title-game rules by season
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.measurement: Maintain a table keyed by (season, conference, team) with membership dates, number of conference games (8 or 9), who plays whom (unbalanced scheduling), title game qualification rule (top two by conference winning percentage with tiebreak order), and champion determination. cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.mechanism: Season-specific table of conference members, number of conference games, title game participants rule and tiebreakers.
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.rationale: Realignment changes the set of teams and the format of every conference contract (for example a reconstituted Pac-12, divisionless Big Ten and SEC, Big 12 title game with the top two teams); a historical conference average built on old membership misprices strengths and tiebreaker paths.

cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.label: Tie probability at the top of a discrete season counting stat
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.measurement: From the joint simulation of end-of-regular-season totals, compute P(max shared by exactly N players) for N = 2, 3. Calibrate by the historical frequency of ties at the top of FBS and power-conference leaderboards for each stat, 2010-2025 regular seasons (NCAA stats), and check the simulation reproduces it within binomial error. Units: probability; sacks evaluated on a 0.5 lattice.
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.mechanism: Probability that two or more players finish the regular season tied for the lead, by stat type: high for passing touchdowns and sacks (small integers; sacks in half units), low for rushing and receiving yards.
cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.rationale: Ties pay $1/N rounded down to the cent, so a candidate's expected payout is P(sole leader) + sum over tie sizes of P(tied in N-way) / N. For passing-TD or sack leaders a two-way tie at, say, 11 sacks is a real event, while for yards it is negligible. Ignoring this mis-values both favourites and long shots.
raw_data: player season stats: player, team, conference, stat totals by regular season

cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.label: Cross-game dependence of leg outcomes through shared rating error
cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.measurement: From joint posterior draws of team ratings (conference offsets kept), compute for each pair of legs the correlation across draws of the win indicators of the BACKED sides, which is determined by the signed exposure vectors e_i (backed conference +1, opposing conference -1, same conference 0) and the offset covariance. Validate empirically by the correlation of signed residuals (actual margin minus non-market expected margin, signed toward the backed team) between games of the same slate, grouped by sign of e_i . e_j, 2014+ postseason and late regular season, shrunk toward zero with prior strength 200 game pairs. Output a signed leg-pair correlation matrix; as-of last completed game.
cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.mechanism: Signed correlation of game-result residuals across different games caused by shared model error: each leg loads on conference offsets with exposure +1 for the backed side's conference, -1 for the opponent's and 0 if both are in one conference.
cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.rationale: Separate games look independent, so the parlay price is usually the product of leg probabilities. But if the rating model over-rates one conference, legs backing it fail together while legs backing its opponents in other games succeed together, so dependence can be positive or negative per pair. In the sampled 4-leg pack a Big Ten error moves Indiana over Alabama and Texas Tech over Oregon in opposite directions, and Georgia over Ole Miss (intra-SEC) is unaffected.
raw_data: games: date, teams, conferences, final margins, neutral flag
own rating posterior draws with conference offsets
backed team and opponent conference per leg

cfb.defender_production_profile.label: Defender production and pass-rush usage profile
cfb.defender_production_profile.measurement: For each defender: sacks, TFL and pressures per pass-rush snap over the last 6 games with weight 0.8 per game, shrunk to a prior-season rate with k = 150 pass-rush snaps; expected snaps remaining = games remaining x snap share (last 4 games); opponent adjustment = opponent offence sacks-allowed rate relative to the FBS mean, with opponent pass attempts forecast from its pass rate; simulate remaining sacks per game as Poisson with a dispersion fit on 2014-2025 and add to the current total; for award votes include team rank and opponent-adjusted havoc rank. As-of the previous Sunday.
cfb.defender_production_profile.mechanism: For defensive voted awards (AP conference Defensive Player of the Year) and sack/tackle-for-loss leaders: the defender share of pass-rush snaps, pressures, sacks, TFL and havoc plays per game against the remaining schedule.
cfb.defender_production_profile.rationale: Defensive votes follow headline sacks and TFL plus team success, and a leader race in sacks depends on pass-rush snap volume, opponent pass-attempt volume and offensive-line quality rather than on rushing or passing efficiency; offence-centric inputs say nothing about it.

cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.label: NFL draft declaration propensity
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.measurement: Logistic hazard on: consensus draft rank (average of public big boards), draft-eligible indicator (years since high school graduation >= 3), draft stock change after the season, college compensation proxy, injury flag, coaching change; calibrate on 2015-2026 declarations using draft early-entry lists; as-of date-specific survival to the announcement window (typically before mid-January). Timestamped public statements are tracked separately.
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.mechanism: Probability that an eligible player announces entry to the NFL draft before the deadline given draft projection, eligibility and alternatives.
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.rationale: The market KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE resolves on a public, unequivocal declaration before Feb 2, 2027; players with high projected picks declare at high rates, but eligibility (three years removed from high school), compensation in college (revenue sharing and NIL), injuries and coaching changes alter the decision, and a statement that a player will return does not count as an early No.

cfb.dst_td_propensity.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown propensity
cfb.dst_td_propensity.measurement: Expected DST TDs per team-game = interceptions forced per game x pick-six rate (shrunk k = 40 INTs to the FBS mean) + fumbles forced x return-TD rate + kick/punt return TD rate for the returner + blocked-kick rate, each opponent-adjusted by the opposing offence's turnover rate; game probability = 1 - exp(-lambda_total) with lambda total = sum of both teams. Kickoff rule regime recorded by season. As-of last game.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.mechanism: Probability that a game contains at least one touchdown scored by a defence or special teams, from turnover returns, kick returns and blocked kicks.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.rationale: DST touchdowns require the opposing offence to turn the ball over in a returnable place or special teams to give returns; they depend on interception and fumble rates, return specialists and the rules for kickoff returns, and are rare events with fat tails.
raw_data: plays with interception, fumble, return, blocked kick and TD flags

cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.label: End-of-regulation decision profile

Output coach-level tie-propensity z-score; coach change resets to prior of coordinators plus career data.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.mechanism: How often a coach settles for a tie (kneel, kick the tying field goal) versus plays for the win in the last two minutes.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.rationale: Tied games are created or avoided in the final minutes: a trailing team that kicks a field goal to tie creates overtime, and a team with the ball tied with 40 seconds left may kneel. Coaches differ systematically, so two matchups with equal margin distributions can differ in tie incidence.

cfb.expected_possessions.label: Expected combined possessions per game
cfb.expected_possessions.measurement: For each team compute average drive duration (seconds) on non-garbage-time drives over last 10 games with 0.8 per-game decay, excluding drives ending a half; expected possessions per team = (3600 - stoppage-adjusted halftime-neutral time) / (0.5*(d_own + d_opp_allowed)) with a clock-regime constant fitted by season; add 1 when either team has no-huddle rate above 40 percent. Report mean and SD (about 2 possessions). As-of the last completed game.
cfb.expected_possessions.mechanism: Number of drives in the game computed from both teams' seconds per drive rather than from averaged plays.
cfb.expected_possessions.rationale: Total points scale with the number of possessions, roughly 22-26 combined in modern FBS games. Seconds per play, plays per drive and run/pass mix interact: two slow teams produce fewer possessions than the average of their individual paces implies, because clock-killing drives are shared.

cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.label: Field-goal attempt and make model by distance
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.measurement: Per team: drives crossing the opponent 35 without scoring a touchdown (count per game, last 10 games with 0.85 decay) x P(kick | 4th down inside 35, distance, score, time) from the coach's historical rates; make probability = logistic(kicker career accuracy by distance bucket with shrinkage k = 20 kicks, wind and temperature adjustment); expected FG made = sum over attempts; add overtime possessions if the contract counts them. As-of pregame kicker and weather vintages.
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.mechanism: Expected number of field-goal attempts per team from drives reaching the 35, decisions to kick, go for it or punt, and probability of making each by distance and weather.
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.rationale: Field-goal counts are attempts times make probability: attempts depend on how many drives stall within range and the coach's 4th-down policy; the make rate depends on distance and conditions; both teams contribute for the total series.

cfb.first_drive.label: Opening-drive tendencies and outcomes

cfb.first_drive.mechanism: Scripted first drives show team-specific tempo, run/pass mix and scoring rates that feed first-quarter and first-TD markets.
cfb.first_drive.rationale: The first drives are pre-scripted and efficient for some teams but the sample per team is small (12-14 games), requiring pooling.

cfb.first_td_race_rate.label: First-touchdown race (hazard and no-touchdown mass)
cfb.first_td_race_rate.measurement: From games since 2014, model time to first TD per team as a piecewise-constant hazard by drive index; hazard depends on team TD per trip, drive pace, opening possession order (receive-first adds probability mass at drive 1) and opponent's early defence; shrink to league hazard with k = 10 games; compute P(team A first) = integral; add P(no TD in 60 min + overtime) from low-total regimes (calibrated on FBS history). As-of kickoff with opening possession probability from cfb.opening_poss. Non-offensive and overtime components: add a defensive/special-teams touchdown arrival hazard per possession of the opponent (from cfb.dst_td_propensity) that can fire before any offensive possession ends; the No-team-scores outcome mass = P(no TD in regulation, from the hazards) x [1 - P(tie after 60 minutes, cfb.ot_model) x P(a touchdown in overtime periods 1-2 | tie)], since the contract settles the first touchdown in the full game including overtime.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.mechanism: Rate at which each team scores its first touchdown, including defensive and special-teams touchdowns, and the probability that neither scores in the full game.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.rationale: First team to score a touchdown is a race between two hazards with a deterministic head start for the receiving team on the opening possession, and with a small chance that neither scores (low-scoring game); overtime still counts for this market.

cfb.fourth_down_aggression.label: Fourth-down aggression and clock-management index
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.measurement: For each head coach, 4th-down go-for-it rate over expected from a fitted model (yard line, distance, score diff, time) = observed go rate - model go rate for the same situations, computed over last 2 seasons with k = 40 situations shrinkage; add mean seconds of clock burned per play when leading by 8-24 in Q4 versus the conference median. Coach change resets to a coach-career prior; compute as-of week.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.mechanism: Coach tendency to go for it, onside, and to run or save clock, which changes margin variance and end-of-game scoring.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.rationale: Aggressive coaches convert field goals into possible touchdowns or turnovers on downs, widening the margin distribution; conservative leaders reduce late scoring. Two teams of equal rating but different aggression produce different cover rates for a rung.

cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.measurement: Define garbage time by margin thresholds above (Q3 > 27, Q4 > 21; verify against published practice); for each team compute points scored and allowed per garbage-time minute and seconds per play when leading, over 2 seasons with 0.5 decay and shrinkage k = 100 snaps; combine with the probability of reaching garbage time from the pre-game rating gap.
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.mechanism: How many points the trailing team and the backups score late when the margin exceeds the garbage-time threshold, and how fast the leader burns clock.
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.rationale: In Q4 totals the effect of a lead is double-edged: the leader scores less and runs the clock, the trailer scores late against backups; the net effect depends on coach pull-point, backup quality and defensive depth, and differs across the 4Q-only and 2H contracts.
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense

cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.label: Goal-to-go and short-yardage run/pass mix
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.measurement: Compute run share on plays inside the opponent 10 and on 3rd/4th-and-short, by team over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season and shrinkage k = 40 plays to the conference mean; add TD conversion rate by type; condition on score state with a logistic model (leading by 14+ increases run share by 0.10-0.15 in the fit). Output expected rushing and receiving TD counts given expected total TDs.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.mechanism: Share of goal-line and short-field plays that are runs (including quarterback sneaks and designed runs) versus passes.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.rationale: Within the same number of touchdowns, the split between rushing and receiving depends on goal-line play calling: option and power-run offences score rushing touchdowns at close range where spread passing offences score receiving touchdowns, and trailing or leading status shifts the mix.
raw_data: plays inside opponent 10 with run/pass and result

cfb.governance_vote_count_state.label: Governance vote count and stakeholder positions
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.measurement: Table of stakeholders with stated position (support, oppose, neutral, undecided) coded from dated public statements, weight by vote power in the governing documents; compute votes in favour needed vs declared; P(approval by deadline) = logistic over (declared share - threshold) and (days left x meeting calendar density); update on each meeting and report; as-of date. Coded manually with source and timestamp.
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.mechanism: Count of declared positions of the decision makers (commissioners, presidents, media partners) against the approval threshold, dated.
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.rationale: CFP expansion to exactly 24 teams (KXNCAAFCFPEXPAND) requires binding approval by the CFP management committee, a body with explicit voting requirements and divided stakeholder positions; the probability of passage depends on how many needed votes are publicly aligned and whether the decision calendar allows approval before the deadline.

cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.label: Half-time state to full-game winner transition matrix
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.measurement: FBS games 2014 onward with quarter line scores. Half margin buckets: <=-15, -14..-8, -7..-4, -3..-1, 0, 1..3, 4..7, 8..14, >=15 (team perspective). Pre-game rating gap from own non-market rating (SP+-style) in 4-point bins plus home/neutral flag and second-half receiver indicator. Fit an ordered logistic of P(win full game | half bucket, gap) with a smooth in gap; shrink each cell toward a bivariate-normal-of-halves baseline with prior strength 60 games. The zero-margin bucket is not fitted here: it is taken from cfb.half_tie_conditional_win (which refines it with the second-half-receiver indicator and owns P(half tied)), so each mechanism has one owner. Output P(full winner | non-tied half bucket) which, multiplied by the half-state probabilities, gives the six cells per game; as-of last completed game before kickoff.
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.mechanism: Conditional probability that each side wins the full game (overtime included) given the first-half margin bucket and the pre-game non-market rating gap; the off-diagonal cells (leader at half loses) are the reversal mass.
cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.rationale: The double result needs the joint of half and full-game outcomes, and reversals are not the product of two marginals: a 10-point half lead by a 14-point underdog is less safe than the same lead by a favourite, and the second-half receiver (usually the team that did not take the opening kick) is not tied to who trails. Independence over-prices favourite/favourite and under-prices underdog-leads/favourite-wins cells.
raw_data: games: game_id, season, week, home, away, neutral_site
line_scores: points by quarter per team
own rating vintages: team, week, rating

free_sources: CFBD plays with EPA and win probability (free key)
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.label: Coach second-half minus first-half efficiency differential
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.measurement: Per head coach and coordinator pair, last 3 seasons: mean (2H - 1H) offensive plus defensive EPA/play from CFBD plays, restricted to plays with win probability 0.10-0.90, opponent-adjusted by opponent season EPA allowed; shrink toward 0 with prior strength 25 games; reset partially (50 percent) on coordinator change. Units: EPA/play; as-of the prior Sunday.
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.mechanism: Persistent tendency of a staff to improve (or fade) after halftime, measured as second-half minus first-half opponent-adjusted EPA per play, net of score-state effects.
cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.rationale: Reputed halftime adjusters shift the reversal cells; most of the raw differential is noise and garbage-time contamination, so it must be measured only in competitive states and shrunk hard. Included as a test of whether staff identity moves the half-to-full transition beyond rating gap.
raw_data: plays: game_id, period, offense, defense, ppa/epa, pre-snap win probability

cfb.joint_path_event_model.label: Joint path events across regular season, title games and CFP bracket
cfb.joint_path_event_model.measurement: From the shared season simulation (20,000 runs, same rating draws as cfb.rating_posterior_draws, conference tiebreaker logic from cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_map, CFP selection and bracket from cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model and cfb.playoff_format): count runs in which the compound condition holds exactly as written (e.g. LSU beats Texas on Nov 14 AND both reach the CFP final AND LSU wins it; specific pair finishes top two and qualifies). Report the probability with its Monte Carlo SE; as-of the latest completed week; no market input.
cfb.joint_path_event_model.mechanism: Joint probability of compound season events, such as a specific pair meeting in a conference title game (KXNCAAFCONFMATCHUP) or the same pair meeting twice with one result each time (KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X), computed inside one season simulation rather than as products of marginals.
cfb.joint_path_event_model.rationale: Compound contracts are dominated by dependence: beating Texas in the regular season raises LSU's chance of making the CFP and lowers Texas's, and a rematch in the national final requires both to win opposite bracket halves; title-game pair contracts require both teams to finish top two under the conference tiebreakers, which are positively or negatively correlated through head-to-head results. Multiplying marginal probabilities misprices these by large factors.

cfb.leader_race_state.label: Statistical-leader race state (current leaderboard plus projected remaining production)
cfb.leader_race_state.measurement: For each candidate, mean per-game production over the last 6 games weighted 0.8 per game, shrunk toward prior-season rate with k = 4 games; adjust per remaining opponent by the opponent's allowed rate (opponent-adjusted), games remaining from the schedule, P(plays) from the hazard input; simulate remaining totals from negative binomial per game with candidate-specific dispersion, add to current total, and compute P(rank 1) with ties allocated 1/N. Update weekly; as-of the previous Sunday.
cfb.leader_race_state.mechanism: Cumulative stat as of the query week for each candidate plus a distribution over remaining production, from usage, efficiency, opponents and games left.
cfb.leader_race_state.rationale: Leader contracts (most rushing yards, passing TDs, receiving yards, sacks) resolve at the end of the regular season on cumulative totals, so the price is an order-statistic problem over several candidates with a current lead, a different number of games remaining and different injury exposure; ties pay $1/N. Note: this id bundles the leaderboard state (current total, gap to rivals, games remaining) with a projection; the state is the input and the overtaking probability is a model output built from it.
raw_data: player game logs with carries, targets, yards, TDs, sacks

cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.label: Leader scoring persistence (points per minute when leading by 14+)
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.measurement: For each team, points scored per minute of game time when leading by 14 or more in Q2-Q4, over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season, relative to the points per minute when within one score; shrinkage k = 60 minutes to the FBS mean; compute also the time of first substitution by backups (depth-chart snap shift) when available. Combine with the probability of reaching a 14-point lead from the rating gap to obtain expected own points.
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.mechanism: How much a team keeps scoring after taking a large lead, versus pulling starters and running the clock.
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.rationale: A heavy favourite's team total lies in the tail of its ability: coaches like some that keep their offence on the field, while others run the ball and substitute early; the same rating produces team totals that differ by 7-10 points depending on persistence. The underdog's mirror image is garbage-time scoring.

backup quarterback and running back snaps

cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.label: Division III and FCS single-game margin model from scores
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.measurement: Shares the score-based team rating of cfb.lower_division_title_model (one rating fit per division, not a second rating; harmonise margin cap, carry-over and home edge with that input) and adds only the single-game layer: ridge-regularised margin rating fitted on all completed games of the division since 2010 (margin capped at 35 points, home edge estimated separately for regular season and playoff, game weight halving every 1.5 seasons, ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out log loss); preseason value = 0.6 x prior final rating shrunk to conference mean; P(win) = Phi((rating gap + home edge) / sigma_div) with sigma_div fitted per division on residuals (expected larger than FBS); posterior SD per team from the ridge Hessian added to sigma_div. As-of the last completed game before kickoff; no market input.
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.mechanism: Win probability for a Division III (KXNCAAFD3GAME) or FCS (KXNCAAFCSGAME) game from a score-based rating difference, a division-specific home edge and a division-specific margin spread, because no play-by-play efficiency or SP+ exists for these teams.
cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.rationale: D3 and FCS winner markets cannot use FBS efficiency ratings: D3 has about 240 teams with almost no out-of-region games before the playoff, so connectivity is weak and rating uncertainty is large; talent gaps are wider than in FBS, so the margin spread is larger and blowouts are common; and the sampled D3/FCS games are playoff games where the higher seed usually hosts, so the home edge must be estimated on postseason games, not regular-season averages.
raw_data: game date, home/away/neutral flag, team ids and division, final score including overtime, playoff round and seed for every D3 and FCS game since 2010

free_sources: NCAA statistics and FCS schedules (free scrape)
cfb.lower_division_title_model.label: FCS, Ivy and lower-division title bracket model
cfb.lower_division_title_model.measurement: Fit an Elo-style rating on FCS (and D3/Ivy) game scores 2014 onward with margin cap 21 points, home-field 2.5 points, preseason carry-over 0.7 shrunk to conference mean, and rating SD from the game count; simulate the conference race (Ivy: record-based, shared title probability reported separately) and the FCS bracket from the announced seeds, 20,000 runs, weekly. Output P(champion) per team and P(co-champion) where applicable. No market input; as-of last completed week.
cfb.lower_division_title_model.mechanism: For FCS, D3 and Ivy League champion markets: team strength from FCS-specific results and the postseason format (FCS playoff bracket and seeds; Ivy League has no title game and awards titles on conference record, possibly shared).
cfb.lower_division_title_model.rationale: FBS ratings (SP+) do not cover these teams; FCS results require their own rating from scores with large mismatch capping, a 24-team bracket with seeds and byes, and the Ivy champion is decided by conference record with possible co-champions, so a market on a single Ivy champion depends on tie handling in the contract (unread, title only).
raw_data: FCS, D3 and Ivy game results
FCS playoff bracket and seeds by season

cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.label: Within-game joint pmf of margin and total at contract strikes
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.measurement: FBS games 2014+: bin by non-market expected margin (3-point bins) and expected total (5-point bins); estimate the joint empirical pmf of (margin, total) on integer lattice with a bivariate kernel smoother centred on a drive-level simulation prior (prior strength 150 games per cell). Evaluate P(margin > -k and total < t) for half-point strikes; report the ratio to the product of marginals as the dependence factor. Overtime points included unless the rules exclude them; as-of kickoff.
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.mechanism: Bivariate distribution of final margin and combined points in one game, given non-market expected margin and expected total, evaluated at the half-point spread and total strikes of a same-game pack.
cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.rationale: A same-game pack such as 'underdog +7.5 and under 48.5' pays on a correlated pair: low-scoring games have compressed margins, so an underdog cover and an under are positively dependent; a favourite cover and an over are positively dependent through blowouts. The dependence changes with the strength gap and with key numbers near 7 and 3.
raw_data: games: final score each team, OT flag
own expected margin and total vintages

cfb.market_ratings.label: Market-implied team strength history
cfb.market_ratings.measurement: Invert closing spreads and totals into team ratings via a ridge/Bradley-Terry fit with home edge by season; keep time-varying ratings and the opener-to-close move; cross-check with SP+ and Elo.
cfb.market_ratings.mechanism: Spreads and moneylines across the season encode sharp information on injuries, QB status and matchups; implied ratings are the strongest prior on team quality.
cfb.market_ratings.rationale: The market is typically well calibrated on spread; the model value is mostly incremental (lineup news, weather, totals) or on props and periods; a rating derived from lines must be tied to the lineup assumed by the line.

cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.label: Large-spread cover curve from non-market rating gap
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.measurement: From historical FBS games (2014 onward), bin pre-game rating gap (non-market, SP+ or own rating) in 3-point buckets; for each bucket compute the empirical survival function P(margin >= k) for k in {1..60} with isotonic smoothing and a beta prior of strength 30 games on the pooled curve. Estimate separate curves for FCS opponents, neutral site, and for coaches in the top and bottom tercile of historical starter-pull time. Output is a vector of probabilities per rung, evaluated as-of kickoff.
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.mechanism: Empirical probability that the favourite's margin exceeds k, as a function of pre-game rating gap and opponent class (FBS vs FCS, G5 vs P4).
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.rationale: Rungs such as FAU by more than 41.5 sit in a regime where starters are removed, the clock runs and margin growth is truncated; a Gaussian around the rating gap overstates the tail, and the truncation point differs for FCS opponents and for coaches who keep scoring.

free_sources: CFBD plays and team stats (free key)
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.label: Net yards per play expectation (rush plus pass, sacks included)
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.measurement: Per team: opponent-adjusted rush yards per attempt with sack and kneel yardage charged to rushing yards (the KXNCAAFTEAMYDS note confirms only this yardage accounting; it does not say sacks count as rush attempts, which does not change total yards), pass yards per attempt, run share expected from script; expected total yards = expected plays x [run share x rush ypc + pass share x (net pass ypa)]; opponent adjustments by opposing allowed values with 10-game window, 0.8 decay, k = 6 games shrinkage; dispersion from historical residuals by bucket. As-of last game.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.mechanism: Expected team total yards from plays times net yards per play, built from rushing and passing components under NCAA accounting.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.rationale: Total yards is plays times yards per play, and under NCAA conventions sack yardage lost is charged to rushing, so net yards per play depends on the sack rate; explosive plays create heavy right tails and yards correlate strongly with pace and script.

free_sources: Beat reporters and coaching carousel trackers (own capture)
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.label: Next-head-coach candidate and timing model
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.measurement: Multinomial logit over the candidate pool with features: current job tier, win rate, school-coach history (alumnus, prior staff), AD's hiring pattern (coordinator vs head coach, G5 head coach), reported interest and visits from timestamped credible reporting (weight by source reliability from past hits), buyout of the candidate's current school; hiring time hazard: P(announce by Sep 1, 2027) from historical time from vacancy to announcement (median weeks). Updated daily.
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.mechanism: Probability that each named person becomes the next permanent head coach, and the timing of the announcement, conditional on a vacancy.
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.rationale: KXNCAAFNEXTCOACH settles on the next permanent head coach officially announced by a date; interim coaches do not count, and the school's tier, athletic director history, available coordinators and head coaches, and leaks determine the distribution. A candidate who is also a candidate elsewhere reduces probability.

cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown rate
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.measurement: For each team: defensive plus special-teams touchdowns scored and allowed per game over 2 seasons with 0.5 season decay, shrunk with k = 12 games toward the FBS mean per team-game (to be measured, plausibly 0.1 to 0.2); add a return-specialist indicator from kick returner yards over expected. Output expected points = 7 x rate (own) + 7 x rate allowed by opponent minus offence replaced.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Rate at which a team scores on interception returns, fumble returns, kickoff and punt returns, and blocked kicks, and allows them.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These touchdowns add 6-8 points without using an offensive possession, are partly skill (returners, ball-hawks) and mostly luck, and fatten the right tail of the total. The market's total rarely prices them separately.
raw_data: plays with type: interception TD, fumble TD, kickoff/punt return TD, blocked kick

cfb.opp_dropback_volume.label: Opposing dropback volume under expected script
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.measurement: Opponent neutral-situation pass rate (first and second down, score within 7, first three quarters) over last 10 games with 0.8 decay, expected plays from state-dependent tempo, and expected score state from non-market ratings (leading by 14+ lowers pass rate by about 10 points; trailing raises it by a similar amount); output expected dropbacks and negative-binomial dispersion. As-of last completed game.
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.mechanism: Expected number of pass dropbacks by the opponent (the opportunity count for sacks and interceptions) given its pass rate and the expected game state.
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.rationale: Sack and interception counts are rates times the opponent's dropbacks, and the opponent's dropbacks swing by 10 to 15 depending on whether it trails or leads; using season averages misprices games with large expected margins. Note: this measures the same quantity as cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts plus cfb.state_dependent_pace in the game_stat_props record (dropbacks under the expected script) and should be aliased to one catalog input.
raw_data: plays with down, distance, score, play type, offense

cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.label: Overtime possession scoring rates (touchdown, field goal, none)
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team: P(TD), P(FG), P(none) on first-and-10 from the 25 with no clock pressure, estimated from non-OT drives starting inside the opponent 30 with shrinkage k = 20 drives plus actual OT possessions with weight 3; opponent-adjust by the same quantity for defences. Period tie probability = sum over outcomes of own x opponent matched scores (TD-TD with equal conversion, FG-FG, none-none). Compute as-of date.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.mechanism: Per-team probabilities of touchdown, field goal or no score from the 25-yard line, offence and defence, opponent-adjusted.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.rationale: Overtime ends when one team outscores the other in a period; probability a period ends tied depends on the pair of scoring outcome distributions, and overtime offence differs from ordinary offence (short field, no clock, kicker at 42 yards).

cfb.own_drive_share.label: Own share of combined possessions
cfb.own_drive_share.measurement: For each team compute its drive share = own drives / (own + opponent drives) in each of the last 10 games, opponent-adjusted by the opponent's mean share allowed, with 0.8 decay and shrinkage k = 5 games to 0.5; add components: average drive duration (own), opponent drive duration allowed, turnover differential per drive. Expected own drives = share x expected combined drives (non-market total pace). As-of last completed game.
cfb.own_drive_share.mechanism: Fraction of the game's total drives that the team receives, after turnovers, special-teams outcomes and the opponent's clock use.
cfb.own_drive_share.rationale: A team's points equal its drives times points per drive; its drive count is not half of the game total because turnover and quick-score differences give one side extra possessions, and a team that burns clock on its own drives reduces the opponent's possessions. A team total rung depends on its own count, not on the average pace.
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock and results

free_sources: CFBD drives with clock fields (free key)
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.label: Combined drives and clock budget per period
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.measurement: For each team compute seconds per non-garbage drive by period (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 separately) over the last 10 games with 0.8 decay; combined drives in period k = 900 / (0.5 (d_a + d_b)) minus end-of-period truncation fraction (empirical 0.1-0.3 drive for Q2 and Q4), with the 2023-onward running-clock regime as a covariate. Output mean and SD of combined drives and P(drives <= 4).
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.mechanism: Expected number of combined drives that fit in the period and the probability that a possession is cut off by the clock.
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.rationale: A quarter holds about five or six combined drives, and the last drive of Q2 and Q4 is truncated by the clock; slow, run-heavy teams can reduce the combined drive count in the first period to four, which lowers the total in a threshold manner at the 7.5 rung.

cfb.period_margin_lattice.label: Period margin lattice and tie mass by expected margin and total
cfb.period_margin_lattice.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 take the line scores by period; for each period and for each of expected-margin bins (-14 to +14 in 3-point bins, from non-market ratings) and expected-total bins (3 bins) estimate P(margin = k) for k in {-14..14} with Dirichlet smoothing (prior strength 100 games, centred on a compound-Poisson model). Evaluate as of kickoff and output joint probabilities of tie, win and cover at each rung.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.mechanism: Empirical probabilities of period margin = 0, positive margins up to 8+, by period and by pre-game expected margin and total.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.rationale: In a single quarter the most likely outcome for evenly matched teams is a tie (0-0 or equal scores) and the winner market loses on ties; spread rungs at 7.5 correspond to a touchdown-plus-two margin or more, so they live in the thin right tail of a lumpy distribution. A Gaussian misprices both the mass at zero and the key numbers.

free_sources: CFBD games and plays (kickoff and coin toss from play text, free key)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.label: Period possession allocation (opening kick, deferral and end-of-half order)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.measurement: Per head coach: P(defer | win toss) over last 3 seasons (shrink k = 10 tosses to the conference mean) and P(win toss) = 0.5; P(team receives first) = 0.5 x P(receive | win) + 0.5 x (1 - opponent P(defer)). Expected drives per quarter per team = season drives per team x quarter share (0.24-0.26 each) with Q1 and Q3 adjusted by the receive-first indicator times 0.5 drive. Store the realised toss only after kickoff.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.mechanism: Expected possessions per team in each quarter given who receives the opening kickoff, deferral habits and tempo.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.rationale: A quarter has only about 2-3 possessions per team, and receiving the opening kickoff gives one extra drive in Q1 (and typically ends Q2 with the other team holding the ball); the share swings expected quarter margin by 0.3 to 0.8 points between the two possession orders. The toss itself is only known at kickoff, so the input must be probabilistic.

cfb.period_share_of_total.label: League-baseline share of scoring by period conditional on expected total and gap
cfb.period_share_of_total.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 compute E[points in period k] / E[regulation points] by bins of expected total (non-market, 4 bins) and absolute expected margin (5 bins), with shrinkage k = 150 games to the pooled share; also store the variance and the share of games with zero points in the period. Apply to the pre-game expected total from a ratings model; exclude overtime from all quarters and add it only to 2H for the 2H contract.
cfb.period_share_of_total.mechanism: Fraction of regulation points scored in each quarter by games with similar expected total and rating gap.
cfb.period_share_of_total.rationale: Allocating a game total to quarters with equal quarters is wrong: end-of-half possessions, scripted openers and lead-dependent second halves make shares unequal and dependent on the gap (blowouts cut Q4 scoring) and on the total. The share is a structural baseline separate from team-specific history.

cfb.period_total_dispersion.label: Period-total dispersion and zero-scoring mass
cfb.period_total_dispersion.measurement: Fit a compound model per period: number of scoring drives N ~ negative binomial with mean mu_k and dispersion r (fit on FBS 2014 onward), points per scoring drive from a 3/6/7/8 mixture with team-specific touchdown share (touchdown share shrunk k = 25 scoring drives). Output P(total = 0), P(total >= 8), and the full pmf up to 28. As-of last completed game. Left-tail validation: on held-out seasons compare predicted P(1H total <= 6), P(2H regulation total <= 6) and P(quarter total = 0) to realised frequencies by expected-total bin (reliability table with binomial intervals); refit the negative-binomial dispersion if the left tail is miscalibrated.
cfb.period_total_dispersion.mechanism: Variance-to-mean ratio and the probability of a scoreless period for team pairs, given expected points.
cfb.period_total_dispersion.rationale: Single-quarter totals are overdispersed relative to Poisson in points but heavily mass-concentrated at 0, 3 and 7; rungs at 7.5 are sensitive to whether the probability of scoring zero in the period is 15 or 25 percent. Explosive teams and field-goal teams differ in the lumpiness for the same mean.
raw_data: scoring drives by period with points

cfb.player_participation_hazard.label: Player participation and season-ending injury hazard
cfb.player_participation_hazard.measurement: Per candidate: P(miss a given game) = base rate by position (estimated from FBS history, to be measured; assume a few percent per game for backs) x workload multiplier (carries per game above the position median) x prior-injury indicator; P(season-ending) as a fraction of misses; combine across remaining games as a Bernoulli path. Redshirt and transfer eligibility flags enter as availability states. Weekly update with timestamped news capture.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.mechanism: Per-game probability that a candidate plays and the probability of a season-ending injury or benching, by position and usage.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.rationale: Contracts resolve to No if the player does not play in the season, and a candidate who misses games falls out of a counting-stat race; running backs and edge rushers have higher injury exposure than quarterbacks and are the main candidates of leader markets.

cfb.poll_release_calendar.label: Poll release calendar and week-label map
cfb.poll_release_calendar.measurement: Table by season: release timestamp, official AP label (Preseason, Week 1..., Final), CFP release Tuesday dates and committee start date; mapping function from contract strings (for example Nov 24, Week 5, Final) to the release that settles it, with the fallback rule next published release after the date; update on announcements; verify against past years. Include the season-by-season AP label table (Preseason, Week 1 ... Week N, Final) because AP Week numbering is AP own label and Preseason is unnumbered, so Week 5 is the fifth numbered release after the Preseason poll; CFP releases are on Tuesdays (Nov 24, 2026 is a Tuesday) with the fallback to the next published release when no release carries the labelled date.
cfb.poll_release_calendar.mechanism: Dates, labels and numbering of AP and CFP releases, including preseason, weekly and final polls.
cfb.poll_release_calendar.rationale: Contracts refer to labelled releases (AP Week 5, Final Rankings expected Jan 26, 2027, CFP rankings of Nov 24, next published after if none is labeled that date); mismatched label dates or an AP week renumbering can resolve a market differently than a naive date match.
raw_data: release dates and labels by season

cfb.poll_transition_model.label: AP poll transition model (rank next week given rank, result and opponent)
cfb.poll_transition_model.measurement: Using AP polls since 1990 (rank, points, first-place votes, week) and game results: for each team-week fit an ordered response model of next rank on previous rank, result (win/loss), margin, opponent's AP rank at the time, home/away, and week of season, with team-level random effects for conference bias; evaluate by rank error. Output distribution over next rank for each team given the simulated weekend. As-of Sunday release.
cfb.poll_transition_model.mechanism: Fitted mapping from the previous AP rank, the weekend result and the opponent to the next AP rank or vote share.
cfb.poll_transition_model.rationale: AP voters start from last week's ballot and move teams for results: a loss by a highly ranked team drops it several places, a win moves it up only if teams above it lose, and unranked teams enter only after notable wins; the preseason poll is built from last year and returning production. Rank is persistent with asymmetric shocks.
raw_data: weekly AP rank, points, first-place votes

cfb.program_trajectory_index.label: Program trajectory index for multi-year contracts
cfb.program_trajectory_index.measurement: Annual team strength follows an AR(1) process: rating_t+1 = mu + 0.7 (rating_t - mu) + shock with shock SD 4 points (placeholder values 0.7 and 4, unsourced and unfitted; to be estimated on 2014-2025 rating changes) augmented by observed 3-year recruiting rank trend, portal net transfer rating change and head-coach tenure/contract status; simulate 4 seasons ahead, add coach-exit hazard and realignment membership, compute P(at least one CFP berth) per path. As-of preseason, updated at the portal window.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.mechanism: Composite of coach tenure, recruiting trend, portal net value, financial resources and past performance for the next four seasons.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.rationale: KXNCAAFTFUT asks whether a team makes the CFP before 2030, which cannot be answered with this year's rating alone: it depends on coach stability, talent pipeline, and revenue-sharing resources over four seasons, and on a random walk of team strength with regression to the mean.

cfb.pythag_luck.label: Close-game record and Pythagorean luck
cfb.pythag_luck.measurement: Pythagorean wins and PPA-based expected wins; one-score game record vs expectation; regress most of the luck.
cfb.pythag_luck.mechanism: Records in one-score games and points-based expected wins deviate from true strength; lucky records regress.
cfb.pythag_luck.rationale: Season futures and rankings based on record overstate lucky teams; Pythagorean/advanced-stat wins are better predictors.

cfb.qb_availability_hazard.label: Starting-quarterback availability hazard and replacement path
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.measurement: Per-game probability that the starter misses a game = base rate estimated from FBS history (to be measured, assume a few percent per game) x mobility/rushing-volume multiplier (designed rushes per game relative to norm) x prior injury history flag; backup rating from prior-year snaps and recruiting composite with shrinkage k = 100 dropbacks; combine in the rating draw to get a mixture over games missed. As-of weekly.
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.mechanism: Probability distribution of quarterback games missed for each contender over the remaining schedule, with the backup's quality.
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.rationale: Top-heavy playoff and title contracts depend on single-quarterback injuries: with an annual per-game miss rate near several percent the chance of losing the starter for at least one game across 12 games is substantial, and the drop to the backup's strength is large; ignoring it makes title probabilities too concentrated.

cfb.qb_interception_propensity.label: Quarterback interception propensity (turnover-worthy plays)
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.measurement: Per QB: expected INT rate = 0.5 x realised INT per attempt (2 seasons, 0.6 decay) + 0.5 x charting-based turnover-worthy rate x conversion factor; if charting unavailable use depth-of-target and completion rate proxy with shrinkage k = 200 attempts; opposing defence adjustment by its INT rate over expected (k = 300 opponent attempts). Multiply by opponent dropbacks (cfb.opp_dropback_volume).
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.mechanism: Expected interceptions per attempt from turnover-worthy throws and depth of target, regressed away from realised interception rate.
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.rationale: Interception rates are noisy: a quarterback with a high realised rate over 150 attempts regresses by about half; turnover-worthy plays and depth of target are more predictive of next-game interceptions than past interceptions, and the defence's ball-hawking skill adds only a small increment.

cfb.qb_replacement_value.label: Quarterback replacement value in points
cfb.qb_replacement_value.measurement: For each team-season, starter value = EPA per dropback (incl. designed rushes) over the last 2 seasons, opponent-adjusted, weighted by dropbacks with a 1-season half-life, shrunk to the recruiting-class prior (247/On3 composite rating mapped to expected EPA/play from historical FBS QBs) with k = 150 dropbacks. Swap value = (starter - replacement) EPA/dropback x team dropbacks per game (about 35 to 45) x 0.75 points per EPA-equivalent play; report mean and posterior SD. As-of timestamp = last confirmed depth-chart or beat-report vintage before kickoff.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.mechanism: Converts a confirmed or doubtful quarterback change into an expected-margin shift in points per game.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.rationale: Identity of the starter (cfb.qb_status_pit) is a vintage, not a number. A backup with 40 career dropbacks has a very wide EPA/play posterior, so the swap cost is both a mean shift and a variance increase; the market tends to over- or under-react depending on prior-year snaps.
raw_data: play-by-play with passer id, EPA, dropbacks

cfb.qb_sack_proneness.label: Quarterback sack proneness independent of line
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.measurement: Per starting QB: sacks per dropback over the last 2 seasons with 0.6 decay, adjusted for opposing pass-rush strength and for pass-block efficiency of his line; decompose into pressure rate x sack-given-pressure; shrinkage k = 150 dropbacks to conference mean; backup quarterback replaced with a recruiting-class prior. As-of pregame QB status vintage.
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.mechanism: Quarterback-specific tendency to take sacks: time to throw, scrambling, holding the ball and sack share of pressures.
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.rationale: Two offences with identical pressure rates can differ in sack rate depending on the quarterback; a mobile quarterback with quick release avoids sacks, a slow decision-maker takes them; for a team sack total the opposing quarterback's contribution is as large as the pass rush.

cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.label: Joint four-quarter scoring pmf with per-team scoreless mass and highest-quarter argmax
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.measurement: From FBS games 2014 onward (CFBD line scores and drives), for each team and quarter fit scoring drives N ~ negative binomial with mean from cfb.q_scoring times expected possessions, dispersion fitted pooled; points per scoring drive from a 3/6/7/8 mixture with team touchdown share shrunk k=25 drives; combine the four quarters with a Gaussian copula whose Spearman correlations are estimated by bins of expected total (3 bins) and absolute expected margin (3 bins), shrunk to the pooled matrix with prior strength 200 games. Simulate 50,000 games: output P(team scores >=1 in quarter k) for each team, the pmf of combined points per quarter, and for QHIGHSCORE the expected payout sum over quarters of P(k is the argmax with N-way tie)/N, Q4 regulation points only. As-of last completed game before kickoff.
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.mechanism: Distribution of each quarter combined points and each team points jointly across Q1-Q4, with quarter-to-quarter correlation, used to price both-teams-to-score in a quarter and the highest-scoring-quarter contract with its 1/N tie split.
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.rationale: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE pays 1/N (rounded down to a cent) when N quarters tie for the most combined points and excludes overtime from Q4; the BTTS series (1Q, 2Q, 3Q) need the per-team probability of scoring at least once in that quarter. Neither is a margin event, so a margin lattice cannot price them: they need the pmf of period totals, the probability each team is held scoreless in the quarter, and the negative dependence between a heavy first half and a compressed second half.
raw_data: line scores by period for both teams

cfb.rating_posterior_draws.label: Correlated rating posterior draws for season simulation
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.measurement: Bayesian rating model fitted to FBS game margins with team-level latent strength, home-field and prior from last season (shrinkage by returning production); draw 4000 posterior samples of the rating vector as of the latest week; for each sample simulate remaining games with game noise SD 13 points and add portal-churn variance inflation to the prior. Keep draw ID for cross-contract consistency.
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.mechanism: Joint posterior samples of all team ratings so that uncertainty is shared across the games of a team and across teams in a conference.
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.rationale: Treating game outcomes as independent given point estimates understates the variance of season totals: a team whose true strength is 3 points above the estimate wins more of every remaining game. Joint draws also propagate connectivity uncertainty across conferences, which matters for conference win counts and playoff selection of Group-of-Five teams.

cfb.rating_posterior_sd.label: Team-rating posterior standard deviation
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.measurement: Bayesian state-space rating per team: prior mean from last season rating x returning-production shrinkage, prior SD 6 points at week 0 falling toward 2.5 by week 10 per the observed rating update; implement as posterior variance = 1 / (1/prior_var + n_eff / game_sd^2) with game_sd = 13 points and n_eff = sum of connectivity-weighted game weights. Add portal-churn variance inflation proportional to 1 - returning production. Use margin-difference SD sqrt(sd_home^2 + sd_away^2 + 13^2 x (1 + 0.3 x pace_variance_term)).
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.mechanism: Per-team uncertainty about true strength given games played, connectivity and roster churn; sets the width of the margin distribution.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.rationale: A rating gap of 7 with SDs of 2.0 and 2.0 gives a different win probability than the same gap with SDs of 5.0 and 5.0 early in the season; ignoring estimation error makes September favourites look too safe and moves cover probabilities at every rung.

cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.label: Realignment feasibility state (grant of rights, exit terms, membership process)
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.measurement: Table by team and conference: grant-of-rights end date, exit fee schedule, notice requirement, membership approval threshold and who votes, litigation status; compute minimal feasible announcement date under current constraints; combine with reported talks (credible reporting count weighted by reliability) in a logistic hazard for announcement in the window; as-of date. Missing terms flagged unknown.
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.mechanism: Contractual and procedural constraints on a conference move: grant-of-rights, exit fees, notice periods, membership votes, litigation status.
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.rationale: Conference leave or join markets (LSU leaving the SEC, Washington State joining the Big 12) resolve on public announcement, binding agreement, formal notice or exit settlement within a window; the feasibility of the move and the steps needed to complete it are much more informative than historical frequencies of realignment.

cfb.regulation_tie_curve.label: Regulation tie probability curve from non-market expected margin and total
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.measurement: From all FBS games since 2005 (about 15,000 games: roughly 750 per season over 21 seasons), fit logistic/GAM of tie indicator on |expected margin| (from SP+ or own rating, not market) and expected total with monotone smoothing; bucket |gap| in 2-point bins (0-2, 2-4, ... 14+) and expected total in 8-point bins; shrink bins to pooled curve with prior strength 200 games. Evaluate as-of kickoff. Output P(tie) with 95 percent interval; for FCS fit separately.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.mechanism: Empirical P(margin = 0 after four quarters) as a function of absolute expected margin and expected total points.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.rationale: A tie is a point mass on a lumpy lattice: the probability is roughly the margin density at zero adjusted for the fact that football scores come in 3, 6, 7, 8 and so ties occur preferentially at combined patterns that are reachable by both sides. The curve is peaked at zero gap and decays quickly, and the expected total changes the margin SD.

cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.label: Remaining-schedule game win probability vector
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.measurement: For each team and each unplayed game compute P(win) = logistic(rating_diff / 13.5 + site_effect) using non-market ratings (SP+ or own, updated through the latest completed week), site effect 2.5 points home / 0 neutral, rest-adjust only for known byes; carry rating posterior SD into correlated draws (see cfb.rating_posterior_draws). Output vector and its Poisson-binomial distribution of wins. As-of the most recent Sunday.
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.mechanism: Game-by-game win probabilities for every unplayed game, from non-market ratings with site, rest and injury state.
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.rationale: Futures contracts on wins, undefeated seasons, conference title and playoff berth are functions of the whole schedule: a team's chance of 12 wins depends on the order, site and quality of each remaining game, and on correlated rating uncertainty; a scalar strength-of-schedule loses the product structure that drives P(undefeated).

cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.label: Points per scoring opportunity (drives crossing opponent 40)
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.measurement: Per team: sum of points on drives with first down inside the opponent 40 divided by number of such drives (over 10 games, 0.85 per-game decay), adjusted by opponent allowed value and by kicker field-goal value; shrink with k = 25 drives toward conference mean. Output mean and SE; combine own offence and opposing defence by an additive deviation model.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.mechanism: Average points on drives that reach the opponent 40 or closer, opponent-adjusted, separating finishing from moving the ball.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.rationale: A team can have strong PPA and still score few points if it settles for field goals; conversely, strong finishers outperform yardage. Scoring-trip efficiency regresses less than red-zone TD rate because it pools more drives and includes field-goal-range situations.
raw_data: drive start/end yard line, result, points scored

cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.label: Script-adjusted team dropbacks
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.measurement: Fit dropbacks per game on team neutral-situation pass rate (first and second down, score within 7, first three quarters), opponent neutral pass-rate allowed, expected margin from non-market ratings (not a quote), and plays; then predict at the pre-game expected margin with a piecewise term at +/-14 and +/-21. Window: current season with 6-game half-life, shrunk to previous season with k = 4 games; as-of the Saturday preceding kickoff. Output: mean attempts and a negative-binomial dispersion.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.mechanism: Expected team pass attempts plus sacks given the expected game flow, rather than the season-average pass rate.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.rationale: Pass volume is the largest driver of receiving-yards variance: a team that trails by two scores throws 50-plus times, a team leading by 21 throws 20. Using season-average attempts mixes games of both kinds and understates the spread in the mean.
raw_data: play-by-play with play_type, down, distance, score diff, period, clock

cfb.script_rush_attempts.label: Script-driven team rush attempts including sacks
cfb.script_rush_attempts.measurement: Rush attempts = plays x run share, where run share = neutral-situation run share (first/second down, score within 7) + lead effect (piecewise: +0.10 when leading by 14+, -0.10 when trailing by 14+) estimated by logistic regression on historical plays, plus sack rate x dropbacks (NCAA convention to be verified in the official stat definition). Opponent run-defence adjust by opponent's attempts allowed; shrink with k = 6 games. As-of last game.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.mechanism: Expected team rushing attempts as plays times run share given the expected lead, counting sacks as rushing attempts under NCAA statistics.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.rationale: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT sits in this archetype and counts a team stat, not points; in NCAA statistics a sack is recorded as a rushing attempt with negative yards, so attempts rise with sack-prone offences, and run share rises sharply for leaders.

cfb.season_max_total_tail.label: Season maximum-total tail model across all Division I games
cfb.season_max_total_tail.measurement: Collect the maximum regular-season Division I total per season 2005-2025 (FBS and FCS games, including overtime) and the full set of per-game totals above 100. Fit a generalised Pareto tail to game totals above 95 points with a threshold chosen by mean-excess plot; scale the exceedance rate by the number of games (about 850 FBS-involved and more with FCS-FCS games) and add a multi-overtime component: P(k overtimes) from cfb.ot_model, with 2-point-only possessions after the second overtime. Output P(max total > K) for K in 120..160 and the number of games expected above 100. As-of date uses only completed seasons plus current-season games already played.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.mechanism: KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE settles on the single largest combined score over every Division I regular-season game including overtime, so it is an extreme-value quantity of roughly 850 game totals, driven by FBS-vs-FCS mismatches, multi-overtime games and pace-and-defence-poor matchups.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.rationale: The rung 144.5 sits far in the tail; the maximum total is governed by rare pairings (two fast, weak defences, or a long overtime game where each overtime adds up to 8 points) rather than the mean total. A Gaussian game-total model badly understates it, so the tail needs an empirical or Poisson-compound fit with a separate overtime-length component.
raw_data: final scores with overtime periods by game 2005 onward

cfb.season_ot_exposure.label: Season overtime exposure (games remaining and current maximum)
cfb.season_ot_exposure.measurement: Count remaining Division I regular-season games as of query date (FBS plus FCS, per the contract's scope) by week; current season maximum number of overtime periods across all D-I games; P(YES) = 1 - (1 - q)^N with q from the tie curve x period-length geometric (with regime change at OT 3), unless max already >= 9 (then 1.0). Update weekly.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.mechanism: Number of remaining Division I games in the regular season and the maximum overtime periods already seen.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.rationale: KXNCAAFMOSTOT is a season-extreme event: if a nine-overtime game has already occurred the market is decided, otherwise the number of remaining games times the per-game probability of reaching 9+ periods determines the price. The decay of exposure through the season is a deterministic input.
raw_data: season schedule with game dates and divisions

cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.label: Second-half overtime spillover
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.measurement: P(OT) from a tie curve (bucketed by non-market expected margin and total) x distribution of OT margin (home/away first possession, points scored by period one: roughly 7 versus 3 versus 0); output expected spillover to the second-half margin = P(OT) x E[OT margin | team] and a variance increment. For 4Q and Q1-Q3 contracts set to zero because they exclude overtime.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.mechanism: Expected effect of overtime on the second-half margin, which includes overtime points by contract.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.rationale: For second-half sides, overtime points are added to each team's second-half total; a game that is tied after regulation is decided by overtime, so the second-half margin equals the overtime result plus second-half regulation margin; ignoring this biases second-half winner probabilities for the close games where it matters.

cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.label: Overtime points increment to the second-half total
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.measurement: P(OT) from cfb.ot_model: logistic/GAM of tie after regulation on absolute non-market expected margin (SP+ or own rating) and expected total, fitted on FBS games 2005 onward with prior strength 200 games. Conditional on OT, combined overtime points = sum over periods of per-possession scoring (touchdown about 0.65 per possession from the 25 with 7 points plus a field-goal share, two-point attempts from the third overtime onward); fit the pmf of combined overtime points on FBS overtime games 2005 onward (about 1,000 games), shrunk to pooled with prior strength 50 games. Output E[increment] = P(OT) x E[OT total] and the pmf to convolve with the regulation 2H pmf. Set to zero for non-2H contracts. As-of last completed game.
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.mechanism: KXNCAAF2HTOTAL counts overtime points, so the 2H total is regulation second-half points plus, with probability P(tied after 60 minutes), the combined points of all overtime periods.
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.rationale: With roughly a 6 percent chance of overtime and around 7 to 10 combined overtime points when it happens, the 2H mean shifts by about half a point and the variance and right tail grow, which matters for a 6.5 rung on a low count; 1Q-3Q, 1H and 4Q contracts exclude overtime and get zero increment.
