cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.label: Snap-weighted availability loss
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.measurement: For each missing or doubtful player i: loss_i = P(out_i) x snap_share_i(prior season or current season to date) x (grade_i - grade_replacement_pos) x positional_points_per_grade, with positional weights fitted from historical snap-weighted ratings (QB >> OT/CB > WR/DL > RB/TE/S). Sum over players, subtract nothing for the opponent. P(out) = 1.0 for confirmed out, 0.5 for doubtful or questionable, 0.15 for unreported-but-flagged. Grades from PFF where available, otherwise PPA-on-field proxy. Timestamp each source report.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.mechanism: Aggregates all known absences (any position) into a single points-per-game value using snap share times player value over replacement.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.rationale: College injury information is sparse, so the model needs a way to price a partial list (two starting linemen out, a corner doubtful) consistently; counting injuries is wrong because snap load and positional value differ by factors of five or more.
raw_data: player snaps by game (PFF or proxy)

cfb.sp_plus.label: SP+/FPI-style composite ratings
cfb.sp_plus.measurement: Pull SP+, FPI, SRS and Elo ratings by week and team; keep the version as of decision time (no revisions); compute rating difference with home adjustment and convert to margin via historical mapping; compare with market-implied margin to see residual.
cfb.sp_plus.mechanism: Published tempo- and opponent-adjusted composite ratings combine efficiency, explosiveness, finishing drives and turnover luck into a strength measure that captures much of team quality.
cfb.sp_plus.rationale: Composite ratings are strong priors and a benchmark for any home-built model; subtle points: their preseason versions rely on returning production and recruiting, and in-season values embed the same noise, so they are not independent from the underlying PPA inputs.

cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.label: Stadium wind exposure and forecast bias
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.measurement: Per stadium: roof type (open, retractable, dome), historical ratio of observed on-field wind (from nearest airport station via NOAA ISD or Meteostat) to forecast at issue 6 hours out, fitted by month over 8 seasons; exposure = ratio x forecast. Outputs adjusted wind in mph and an indicator of >15 mph. Apply only at kickoff plus 3 hours.
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.mechanism: Translates a forecast wind speed into expected on-field wind by stadium (open bowl, enclosed, dome, orientation).
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.rationale: A 20 mph forecast at a closed or dome stadium is irrelevant while the same forecast at an open lakeside stadium cuts passing and field-goal range materially; the forecast vintage alone is not predictive without the exposure factor.
raw_data: venue table with roof, orientation, lat/long

cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.label: Joint end-of-regular-season simulation of all eligible contenders

For each, per-game production ~ negative binomial (yards: gamma on carries/targets x per-opportunity yards) with mean built here from cfb.player_usage share x script-adjusted team volume x per-opportunity efficiency adjusted by cfb.dvp for each remaining opponent (cfb.leader_race_state supplies only current totals and games remaining, so projection happens once) and dispersion fitted per position; shared team shock (log-normal SD fitted from team pace residuals) and teammate usage constraint (team carries or targets fixed per simulated game). cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.mechanism: Monte Carlo of remaining regular-season production for every player in the conference (or, for the national series, Division I: FBS plus FCS contenders while C-U2 is open) with a realistic chance, including teammates who share usage and players not listed as markets, with team-level shocks shared within a team.
cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.rationale: Leader probability is an order statistic over the whole field. Pricing listed names alone over-states each; teammates (RB1/RB2, two WRs) are negatively correlated through shared usage, while players on the same team share positive shocks from team pace and QB health. Remaining-game counts differ by team (byes already taken, Hawaii 13-game exemption, cancelled games), and conference title games do not count.

raw_data: touchdowns by game and team and type

cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.label: Touchdowns per scoring trip (drives reaching opponent 40) with type split
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.measurement: For each team: trips = drives with a first down at or inside the opponent 40; TD per trip over last 10 games with 0.85 decay, opponent-adjusted by the opponent defence's TD per trip allowed, shrinkage k = 25 trips to the FBS mean; split of TDs by type (rush, pass, other) over 2 seasons with shrinkage k = 30 TDs. Expected team TDs = expected trips x TD per trip; variance from negative binomial with fitted dispersion.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.mechanism: Expected touchdown count from the number of drives reaching scoring range and the touchdown conversion rate, split into rushing, receiving and non-offensive.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.rationale: All live series count touchdowns, not points: a drive that ends in a field goal produces no TD, so TD count depends on finishing (TD versus FG versus turnover) more than on points; the type split determines TEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD.
raw_data: drives with start/end field position and result
scoring plays with type (rush, pass, return)

cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.label: Own-versus-opponent score covariance
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.measurement: From FBS games since 2014, compute residual correlation between team points and opponent points after removing expected team points from non-market ratings, by bin of expected margin (-14 to +14) and expected total; shrink bin correlations to pooled correlation with k = 150 games. Use the covariance matrix to turn a game-level total and margin model into a joint bivariate distribution; check consistency with the team total ladder. Functional form: team points as negative-binomial scoring-drive counts joined by a Gaussian copula with rho = rho0 + rho1 x |expected margin| + rho2 x expected total (coefficients fitted by maximum likelihood on FBS 2014 onward; the sign change of rho is a hypothesis to test, not an assumption). Tail check: validate P(team points > 45) calibration on held-out games with expected team points above 38, since rungs like 45.5 sit in the far right tail.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.mechanism: Covariance between a team's points and its opponent's points given the expected margin and total.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.rationale: Own and opponent scores are positively correlated through pace and negatively through script and clock control, so the variance of own points depends on the regime; a team total over 45.5 is more likely in shootouts where both score, and less likely when the opponent runs the clock.

free_sources: CFBD games, drives and PPA (free key)
cfb.team_period_points_share.label: Team share of period points from non-market team strengths
cfb.team_period_points_share.measurement: Expected 1H points for team A = (E[game 1H points] from cfb.period_share_of_total) x w_A, with w_A = A expected game points / (A + B expected game points) where expected points come from opponent-adjusted off_ppa and def_ppa (current season with 6-game half-life shrunk to prior season with k=4 games), then add 0.5 x A points per drive if A receives the first-half kickoff and subtract 0.5 x B points per drive if B does not receive. Output mean and a negative-binomial scoring-drive dispersion fitted on FBS 2014 onward. As-of the Saturday preceding kickoff; no price or line input.
cfb.team_period_points_share.mechanism: Splits the game-level expected points in a half between the two teams using each offence points per drive against the opposing defence, plus the receiving team in the half, for KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL.
cfb.team_period_points_share.rationale: The team-side 1H total is not half of a team full-game total: the share depends on who receives the opening kickoff and which team has the stronger offence against the weaker defence, and first-half scoring is lumpy. Without a non-market allocation the series would need the benchmark team-total split.
raw_data: team points per drive and opponent-adjusted PPA

cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.label: National-title path probability and AP final-ranking link
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.measurement: Simulate the bracket 20,000 times from cfb.sp_plus-type non-market ratings with posterior SD (as in the season_futures simulation): seeding from a projected committee ranking (cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features), bracket paths under the 2026 format, neutral-site games without home edge; output P(national champion) per team. Then P(AP final #1 = team) = P(champion) x P(AP #1 | champion; empirical rate from CFP-era seasons with Beta(9, 1) prior) + P(non-champion #1 | split cases, small mass from the same history). As-of the latest week; update after each bracket round.
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.mechanism: KXNCAAFAPRANK (Final AP #1, released after the title game) and the late-season paths of KXNCAAFAPANY and KXNCAAFAPCHURN depend on bowl and CFP results through the national championship; the input is a bracket simulation from non-market ratings plus the historical link between the CFP champion and the AP final #1.
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.rationale: The Final AP poll is released after the championship game (rules text: Final Rankings expected Jan 26, 2027), so the leading candidate for #1 is the CFP champion; AP voters have ranked the champion first in the CFP era (2014-2024, to be verified), which turns the Final-#1 market into a title-probability market with a small split-vote tail, and the number of distinct #1 teams depends on regular-season losses of the top-ranked team before the bracket.
raw_data: historical AP final rank vs CFP champion

cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.label: Top-team loss hazard and number-one succession simulation
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.measurement: For each top-8 team compute weekly P(loss) from non-market ratings and game site; simulate the AP number-one chain: leader loses -> successor by ballot_points_gap softmax; leader wins -> stays unless voters swap (historical swap rate to be estimated); produce P(distinct number-ones >= k) and P(team i ever #1). Correlation via shared rating draws and head-to-head constraints. As-of latest week, including preseason poll.
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the current number one (and the next few teams) lose in each remaining week, combined into a succession process.
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.rationale: Distinct-number-one and any-week-number-one markets are driven by upsets of the few top teams: each week the number one has a 5-20 percent chance to lose depending on opponent and venue, and the count of distinct number-ones grows by one per succession; head-to-head games between top teams guarantee a loser.

cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.label: Transfer destination candidate model
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.measurement: State machine: P(enters portal) from player class, role, coach change, depth chart competitor and reported interest; conditional destination multinomial with features (position need, revenue-sharing capacity estimate, coach relationship, region, visits) from timestamped credible reports; window dates from NCAA rules; as-of date. Missing compensation data imputed from conference tier.
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.mechanism: Probability over destinations for a named player: stays, declares for the draft, or commits to a specific school, from portal status and reported interest.
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.rationale: KXNCAAFTRANSFER offers multi-outcome markets (stays, declares for the draft, commits elsewhere); resolution depends on the portal window, whether the player enters, and which programs have need and compensation capacity; staying resolves YES if the player withdraws from the portal.

free_sources: CFBD plays and drives with clock (free key)
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.label: Two-minute and end-of-half drive efficiency
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.measurement: For each team: points per drive in the last 2:00 of Q2 and Q4 when score within 14 and at least one timeout, over 2 seasons, with 0.5 decay per season and shrinkage k = 20 drives to the conference mean; include kneel-down rate (drives ending in kneels when leading) and no-timeout slot. Compute opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed value.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.mechanism: Points per drive in the final two minutes of the first half and of the game, plus the share of drives where the leader runs out the clock.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.rationale: Quarters 2 and 4 end with clock-driven scoring chances that are not representative of normal drives; a good two-minute offence with a reliable kicker produces points at a much higher rate, and teams differ in whether they play to score or hold the ball at the end of the half.
raw_data: drive records with start time, clock at start, timeouts, result

cfb.two_point_attempt_model.label: Two-point attempt decision and success model
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.measurement: Per coach: P(go for 2 | TD, score diff, period) from a logistic fit on 2014-2025 plays, with shrinkage k = 20 touchdowns to the conference mean; success rate by team offence and opposing defence, beta prior at league mean (to be estimated) with strength 25; expected successful regulation conversions = expected touchdowns x decision probability x success rate (overtime excluded by the contract); output P(at least one successful) and the count pmf. As-of pregame.
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.mechanism: Number of touchdowns times the probability of going for two (by score chart and coach) times success rate from the 3-yard line.
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.rationale: Two-point conversions are a small count: 0 to 3 per game, and under KXNCAAF2PT only successful conversions in regulation count. Attempts follow the touchdown count, the score differential (chart situations such as down 8 or up 17 invite a try) and the coach's tendency; success rate is near one half but depends on the offence and defence.
raw_data: touchdowns and extra-point/2-point attempts with score state

free_sources: CFBD plays: two-point conversion play types (free key)
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.label: Two-point conversion success rate for the alternating-attempt overtimes
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.measurement: Per team: successful two-point attempts divided by attempts, offence and defence, over 3 seasons with beta prior at league mean of roughly 0.47-0.50 (to be estimated) and prior strength 25 attempts; use goal-to-go 3-yard plays with 2 or fewer yards to go as proxy where attempts are few. Combine as p_a = (off_a + (1 - def_b)) / 2. As-of date.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.mechanism: Team probability of converting a two-point attempt from the 3-yard line, offence and defence, used from the third overtime.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.rationale: From the third overtime onward periods are single two-point attempts; a period ends tied whenever both teams convert or both fail, so the per-period tie chance is p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b), close to one half for any plausible p, which keeps the process nearly memoryless and makes 9+ periods a power of about one half.
raw_data: two-point attempts with result and play type

cfb.victory_formation_yardage.label: Victory-formation and end-of-half kneel yardage loss
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.measurement: From play-by-play 2014 onward, classify kneels (play text contains 'kneel' or rush of -1 to -3 yards with zero time-out usage in the final 2:00 of a half while leading or tied); estimate P(kneel series | expected lead at 2:00 of the 4th quarter and of the 2nd quarter), using the team kneel-down rate already defined in cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency as the team-level prior rather than re-estimating it, by logistic fit on the non-market expected margin, and mean yards per kneel series (count of kneels x mean loss, about -1 to -2 yards each). Expected kneel yards = sum over halves of P(series) x mean loss; as-of kickoff.
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.mechanism: Expected negative rushing yardage from quarterback kneels at the end of a half or game, which the KXNCAAFTEAMYDS note charges to the offence's rushing (and so total) yards.
cfb.victory_formation_yardage.rationale: The rules make kneels negative rushing yards, so a team that leads late loses a few yards per kneel series; the loss is near zero for trailing teams and concentrated in the favourite's distribution, slightly shifting rung probabilities near the strike for teams expected to win comfortably; it also lowers rushing attempts' yards per carry.
raw_data: play-by-play: play_type, play_text, yards_gained, period, clock, offense score, defense score

free_sources: NOAA GOES-R GLM lightning data (free, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED archive convenience)
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.label: Weather delay hazard from thunderstorm and lightning forecast
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.measurement: P(delay) = logistic of forecast probability of thunderstorms in the 4-hour window, convective available potential energy index, local time (afternoon peak), month, roof status, and prior delay frequency at the stadium; calibrated on historical games with documented delays since 2010. Forecast vintage within 6 hours of kickoff; update with live radar if allowed. Event definition per the series rules: any official weather delay, including a delayed start or any suspension or stoppage after kickoff, with no minimum duration.
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.mechanism: Probability of a stoppage from lightning or severe weather during a window around kickoff given forecast thunderstorm probability, lightning proximity and venue protocol.
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.rationale: A weather delay is a binary event driven by lightning within a protocol radius (about 8 miles under common policy) and the 30-minute clock that restarts with each strike; early-season Southern and Midwestern afternoon games are most exposed, and domes and closed stadiums remove the risk.

cfb.wr_personnel_rate.label: Receiver personnel-grouping rate
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.measurement: For each offence, share of snaps by personnel group (RB/TE/WR counts) over the last 8 games, opponent-weighted; compute the 3+ WR snap share and empty-set rate with k = 150 snap shrinkage to conference average. Combine with receiver snap shares and starters out as of the pregame vintage.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps with 3 or more receivers (11 personnel, 10 personnel, empty sets) versus heavy sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.rationale: Receiving-yards volume depends on how many pass-catchers are deployed: spread offences convert dropbacks into more targets to receivers and fewer to backs and tight ends, and the loss of a receiver matters more when the team lives in 4-wide sets.

free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)
m.stat_source_mismatch.label: Official versus provider stat definition and source mismatch
m.stat_source_mismatch.measurement: Compare player/team stats across at least two sources for completed games and record mismatch rates by stat; identify the contract source and lock time; flag ladders where realized values fall within typical mismatch tolerance.
m.stat_source_mismatch.mechanism: College statistics differ across sources (NCAA official, ESPN, school stat crews) and in definitions (sack yardage counted against rushing, bowl and conference game inclusion), so thresholds near a boundary can resolve differently.
m.stat_source_mismatch.rationale: Stat props resolve on a named source; if the model is trained on another source the label is wrong; corrections after the game and differences in treatment (kneel-downs, sacks) are sources of tail risk especially around round thresholds.
